cards.html: This skill is the decision: when Firebase is the right tool, when it is not, and what else you could use.

• You are a small team or one person and need auth, data and push this week, with no backend to run.
  • The data is document-shaped and driven by the app (profiles, notes, chats, to-do lists), with few cross-document queries.
  • You want real-time sync or offline support almost for free.
  • Your users are mostly on mobile, where the SDKs are strongest.
  • You want a free crash reporter and analytics source for a published app.

cards.s: Do not use Firebase (or not that part) when
cards.html:
• Your data is relational and you need joins, multi-row transactions or ad-hoc SQL reporting. Firestore will fight you; use Postgres.
  • You already run a backend and database that work. Adding Firestore creates two sources of truth. Take only the leaves (push, Crashlytics, Hosting).
  • You cannot accept vendor lock-in on the data layer, or you must self-host or meet a data-residency rule you cannot satisfy.
  • Your read patterns are large and unpredictable, so per-operation billing is a risk you cannot cap.
  • You need heavy server-side compute or ML serving. Functions are for glue.

OptionBest whenBreaks whenCost and complexity
Own backend (FastAPI and Postgres)You want control, SQL and portabilityYou are one person who must also run itYour time; hosting is small and predictable
FirebaseSmall team, mobile app, real-time or offlineRelational data, unpredictable reads, must stay portableFree to start; database billed per operation; high lock-in
Supabase (Postgres, auth, storage, open source)You want Firebase's speed but SQL and an exitYou need Firebase's mobile offline maturityHosted tiers or self-host; lower lock-in [depends]
Appwrite or PocketBase (self-hosted)You want to own the boxYou cannot operate a serverFree software; you run and patch it
A cloud provider's mobile backend (such as AWS Amplify)You are already deep in that cloudYou want Firebase's simple SDKsPowerful, with more moving parts
Keep your backend, add only FCMA working backend that needs pushYou wanted a whole backend replacedNear zero; the lowest lock-in

LevelUp already has a FastAPI backend, its own accounts, progress stored per learner, and a tested merge for offline edits.

  • Authentication and Firestore would duplicate the accounts and the progress store and create a second source of truth. Skip them.
  • Hosting is already covered by Caddy.
  • FCM is the one thing the app lacks: nudges wait for a 15-minute poll today.

Verdict: adopt only FCM, keep the user-to-token table in the existing backend, and revisit Crashlytics when there is a published app. It is the cheapest, lowest-lock-in answer.

quiz.q: When is Firebase the wrong choice?
o: Your data is relational and you need joins and SQL reporting
A small mobile app with document-shaped data
You want a free crash reporter

quiz.q: You already run a working backend and only lack push. The best move is …
o: add only FCM and keep your own backend
quiz.why: Take only what you lack; avoid two sources of truth.

quiz.q: Which alternative offers Postgres with auth and storage, and is open source?
quiz.why: It gives Firebase-like speed with SQL and an easier exit.

quiz.q: For LevelUp, which Firebase product does the guide recommend adopting?
quiz.why: Auth and Firestore would duplicate accounts and progress.
